science.title: Preliminary evaluation of a qPCR HRM assay for differentiation of Leishmania major and Leishmania tropica
science.description: Rapid and accurate identification of Leishmania species is important for the diagnosis and epidemiological surveillance of cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL). High-resolution melting (HRM) analysis has emerged as a rapid molecular approach for species discrimination. This study aimed to preliminarily evaluate a quantitative real-time PCR coupled with HRM (qPCR-HRM) assay targeting kinetoplast minicircle DNA (kDNA) for differentiation of Leishmania major and Leishmania tropica in northeastern Iran. A qPCR-HRM assay targeting the kDNA region was developed using species-specific primers. Clinical samples from 60 patients with suspected CL in North Khorasan and Razavi Khorasan provinces were examined microscopically and cultured. DNA extracted from cultured promastigotes was analyzed using qPCR-HRM, and the results were compared with conventional PCR and ITS1-rDNA sequencing. In addition, ITS1-rDNA sequence analysis was performed to evaluate the genetic diversity of L. major isolates. Among the 60 suspected CL samples, 13 were positive by molecular analysis. qPCR-HRM successfully differentiated reference strains of L. major and L. tropica based on distinct melting temperature profiles, with a mean ΔTm of approximately 0.86 °C (L. major: 84.13 °C; L. tropica: 83.27 °C). All clinical isolates were identified as L. major by qPCR-HRM and confirmed by ITS1 sequencing, showing complete agreement between the two methods. ITS1-rDNA analysis of the 13 L. major isolates identified nine sequence types and seven haplotypes. The qPCR-HRM assay demonstrated promising performance for rapid differentiation of L. major and L. tropica under the conditions evaluated in this study. However, further validation using larger numbers of direct clinical specimens representing both species is required before routine diagnostic application.

science.title: Photo-induced interfacial charge transfer in solar-responsive PVDF composite membranes
science.description: Solar-driven membrane distillation (SDMD) using advanced composite membranes offers promise for sustainable water purification. Here, we present an atomistic computational study of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membranes incorporating hexagonal boron nitride (BN) and tungsten nitride (WN) nanofillers to elucidate the mechanisms underlying photoinduced charge transfer and photothermal excitation. We use a hierarchical multiscale framework integrating density functional theory (DFT), time-dependent DFT perturbation theory, and classical molecular dynamics to assess the electronic, optical, and structural properties of PVDF/BN/WN composites. Our calculations reveal a dramatic narrowing of the band gap from pristine PVDF (5.41 eV) to 0.57 eV in the composite, driven by orbital hybridization and enhanced interfacial charge transfer. Low-energy optical absorption (~ 0.85 eV) associated with charge-transfer transitions and collective excitations in WN clusters, alongside broadband activity from the near-infrared to the ultraviolet, is predicted. Molecular dynamics simulations confirm structural stability and strong interfacial ordering, with realistic atomic densities and constrained polymer mobility. These findings provide quantitative insight into the interplay between nanofiller-induced electronic structure modulation and membrane stability, establishing a theoretical foundation for designing PVDF-based composite membranes for efficient solar-driven water purification and related energy applications.
